transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (CTO, Southwind), Mark Bennett (Head of Security), Suresh Patel (DevOps Lead)

Summary: quick intro then deep dive on security posture, compliance, and integration requirements. Team asked for SOC2 report, SAML guide, KMS options, and audit log retention specifics.

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. With me is Liam, our SE. How are you all?
[00:08] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Doing well, thanks. I'll let Mark and Suresh chime in on the security specifics.
[00:12] Mark Bennett: Hi, thanks. We, uh, at Southwind are evaluating options for hosting inference. Primary must-haves are SOC2 or ISO evidence, SSO/SAML, strong RBAC, and long-term audit logs.
[00:24] Liam Chen: Totally — thanks Mark. We usually start by mapping requirements to our product modes: Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). Each has different controls around network and key management.
[00:36] Suresh Patel: Quick question, at a high level: is encryption at rest managed by Redwood for Hosted, and can we bring our own KMS for Dedicated/Private?
[00:44] Maya Patel: Great question. For Hosted, Redwood manages keys by default but we offer customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we do envelope encryption with provider-managed keys unless you request a dedicated config — there's an enterprise add-on for that.
[01:00] Mark Bennett: And the SOC2? We need Type II report for last 12 months, plus ISO 27001 scope. Do you have current certs?
[01:09] Maya Patel: We're SOC 2 Type II as of last quarter — I'll send the report. We also have an ISO 27001 summary and the scope doc. I'll follow up with the artifacts after the call.
[01:20] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Great. On SSO — our IdP is Okta. We need SAML 2.0 support and SCIM for user provisioning, also RBAC to map roles from SCIM groups.
[01:32] Liam Chen: Okta's a common integration — Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and SCIM. For RBAC we expose roles like Admin, Dev, Viewer, and you can map IdP groups to those roles. There are a couple of nuances around service accounts and API keys we should cover.
[01:45] Suresh Patel: Specifically, can we restrict access so only certain subnets from our VPC can reach the Dedicated instance? We're concerned about lateral movement and want strict network controls.
[01:55] Liam Chen: For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and allowlist IP ranges; Private gives more control with customer-managed networking and optional on-prem install. We can lock it down to specific subnets and enforce security groups, but we'll need your network diagram.
[02:10] Mark Bennett: Audit logs — how long do you retain them, and can we push logs to our SIEM? We need 12 months of immutable logs for audit.
[02:20] Maya Patel: By default Hosted retains logs 90 days. For Dedicated/Private we can configure longer retention and export via secure S3 or syslog to your SIEM. For immutable retention (WORM-like) we can discuss long-term archival — it's an enterprise add-on.
[02:33] Dr. Elena Ruiz: What's in the audit trail? API keys usage, request/response metadata, redaction details? We can't retain PHI in plain text.
[02:43] Liam Chen: The audit logs include authentication events, token usage, model/version deployed, request metadata, and non-sensitive request headers. Request/response bodies are sensitive — by default we store metadata, not full payload; for cases where you need full-text logs we recommend redaction or client-side encryption.
[03:00] Mark Bennett: Hmm, client-side encryption — so we could encrypt payloads before sending and Redwood would see a cipher blob? That would impact model utility though.
[03:09] Suresh Patel: Right, that kills usefulness. We need to figure out a middle ground: maybe PII redaction before sending?
[03:15] Maya Patel: Exactly. Many customers use tokenization or deterministic redaction in their app layer. For some workflows, Dedicated with customer-managed KMS gives a balance: keys are controlled by you and decrypted in a secure enclave so we limit exposure.
[03:30] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Can you explain the KMS flow for Dedicated? If we choose AWS KMS, do we manage grants and keys, and how are they rotated?
[03:39] Liam Chen: If you bring AWS KMS we integrate via cross-account roles and you keep the key. Redwood requests decrypt permissions at runtime. Rotation is managed by you on the KMS side; we recommend key rotation policies and we can provide guidance for minimal downtime.
[03:52] Mark Bennett: Do you have penetration test reports or can we conduct our own while under NDA?
[03:58] Maya Patel: We have an annual pentest report summary; we can share a redacted summary. We also sign customer NDAs and allow security teams to run scoping tests — there is a standard process with timelines.
[04:10] Suresh Patel: For network — if we pick Dedicated, what's the deployment time and what's the required topology? We need to know firewall rules and egress controls.
[04:20] Liam Chen: Typical Dedicated provisioning is 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and region. We'll send a deployment checklist with CIDRs, ports (e.g., 443 outbound to control plane endpoints), and required tunnels for private deployments.
[04:34] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Ok. Another point — data residency. Our data must remain in the EU for certain workflows. Do you offer region pinning?
[04:43] Maya Patel: Yes, region pinning is supported. Hosted can be region-scoped; Dedicated and Private give you full control. We'll note required EU-only deployment for the pilot.
[04:53] Mark Bennett: Anything about RBAC granularity — can we audit role changes and have a history?
[04:58] Liam Chen: Yes, role changes and admin events are included in the audit trail. For Dedicated we can keep longer retention and provide export hooks.
[05:06] Maya Patel: Let's talk gaps vs Hosted: Hosted is fastest to start but has managed keys and shorter default log retention. Dedicated gives isolated compute and ability to plug into your KMS and networking. Private/on‑prem gives the most control but is more work to set up.
[05:20] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Sounds like Dedicated is our sweet spot — want the isolation and yet some management overhead. We'll need pricing and a clear path for KMS and SSO integration.
[05:29] Mark Bennett: Also want to confirm: in Dedicated, are model weights ever accessible to Redwood engineers?
[05:35] Liam Chen: Model weights are stored on the host; Redwood ops has limited operational access under strict, audited procedures. For Private/on-prem, you can fully control access. We can provide a write‑up of access controls and privileged access processes.
[05:47] Suresh Patel: For the pilot, can we do a synthetic benchmark that includes 1k concurrent requests and 95th percentile latency targets? We want to validate throughput and latency for our common prompts.
[05:57] Liam Chen: Yes, we'll provide a benchmark harness. For Dedicated we'll propose a capacity profile and we can run it together during the pilot.
[06:05] Maya Patel: I'll include the benchmark script in the follow-up and propose dates for the infra deep dive.
[06:10] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Perfect. Any other questions from our side?
[06:14] Mark Bennett: One small thing — does Redwood offer SSO session timeout policies and ability to enforce MFA via IdP?
[06:22] Liam Chen: Session timeouts are policy-driven from the IdP side; we honor SAML session lifetime and you can enforce MFA through your IdP. We also support forced reauth for sensitive operations.
[06:33] Suresh Patel: On log export — can we forward logs in near real-time to our SIEM, or is it batch?
[06:38] Maya Patel: We support streaming logs to SIEM via secure syslog or pushing to customer S3 with event notifications; near real-time streaming is available for Dedicated.
[06:47] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Ok, that helps. Anything else from Redwood?
[06:50] Maya Patel: Next steps: we'll send SOC2 and ISO artifacts, SAML guide, deployment checklist, and pricing. Liam will schedule the infra deep dive. Also we can get an NDA in place for any deeper pentest docs.
[07:03] Mark Bennett: Thanks, please include the specific contact for security review. I'll be the point for that.
[07:08] Maya Patel: Noted — Mark as security POC.
[07:11] Liam Chen: I'll reach out to Suresh directly to lock in times and get the network diagram.
[07:16] Suresh Patel: Sounds good.
[07:18] Maya Patel: Great \u2014 thanks everyone. We'll follow up by tomorrow with the artifacts.
[07:23] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Appreciate it.
[07:25] End of recording.

Notes on transcription: some small transcription errors possible (proper nouns, minor pauses), but overall captures Q&A and action items.
